lessons.title: Ieri ho…
lessons.outcome: Say what you did with avere and a past participle.

activities.body: To say what you did, use the present of avere (ho, hai, ha, abbiamo, avete, hanno) and the past participle: -are → -ato, -ere → -uto, -ire → -ito.

examples.en: Yesterday I ate pizza.
Did you see the film?
Marco slept a lot.
We bought the newspaper.

activities.tip: The subject pronoun is usually dropped: ho mangiato already says who. Irregular participles to know: visto (vedere), fatto (fare), letto (leggere), bevuto (bere), preso (prendere).

activities.en: Yesterday I ate pizza.
activities.explanation: Mangiare takes avere (ho, not sono), and after ho comes the participle mangiato, never the infinitive.

activities.en: Last night I watched a good film.

blanks.explanation: Io takes ho. Vedere has the irregular participle visto; guardare is regular: guardato.

activities.hint: Who watched the film? You did.

activities.en: Marco slept all day.

blanks.explanation: -ire verbs make the participle in -ito: dormire → dormito. After ha comes the participle, never the present or the infinitive.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.en: Hi! What did you do yesterday?

turns.speaker: you
turns.en: Yesterday I ____.

blanks.explanation: Talking about yourself: ho + participle. Fare has the irregular participle fatto.

reactions.it: Un film! Al cinema o a casa?
reactions.en: A film! At the cinema or at home?

reactions.it: Tutto il giorno? Che peccato!
reactions.en: All day? What a pity!

reactions.it: Bene! Io invece ho dormito poco.
reactions.en: Good! I slept little instead.

reactions.it: Anche io ho fatto la spesa!
reactions.en: I did the shopping too!

reactions.it: Capisco. Io ho letto un libro.
reactions.en: I see. I read a book.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.it: E oggi? Hai già fatto colazione?
turns.en: And today? Have you had breakfast yet?

turns.speaker: you
turns.en: Yes, I ____ a cappuccino.

blanks.explanation: Prendere → preso and bere → bevuto are irregular participles; the auxiliary is still ho.

reactions.it: Un cappuccino! Buona idea.
reactions.en: A cappuccino! Good idea.

reactions.it: Anche io ho bevuto un cappuccino.
reactions.en: I drank a cappuccino too.

reactions.it: Perfetto. Allora andiamo!
reactions.en: Perfect. Then let's go!

turns.speaker: partner
turns.en: Come on, let's go to work.

activities.en: Did you see the film?
activities.explanation: Tu takes hai. With avere the participle visto does not change.
activities.hint: A question keeps the same word order.

activities.template: Noi ____ il pane e loro ____ il vino.
activities.en: We bought the bread and they bought the wine.

blanks.explanation: Noi takes abbiamo: abbiamo comprato.
Loro takes hanno: hanno comprato.

examples: Io ho mangiato la pizza ieri.
Mia madre ha comprato il giornale.
Noi abbiamo visto un film ieri sera.

lessons.title: Sono andato
lessons.outcome: Say where you went with essere and a participle that agrees with you.

activities.body: Verbs of movement and change (andare, arrivare, uscire, tornare), and essere itself, take essere. The participle then agrees with the subject: andato, andata, andati, andate.

examples.en: I went to the seaside. (a man speaking)
Maria arrived late.
We went out with friends.

examples.it: Le ragazze sono tornate a casa presto.
examples.en: The girls came home early.

activities.tip: A woman says sono andata, a man sono andato. A mixed group uses -i: siamo andati. Essere itself uses stato: sono stato a Roma, sono stata a Roma.

activities.en: Maria arrived late at the station.
activities.answer: Maria è arrivata tardi alla stazione.
activities.explanation: Arrivare takes essere, never ha. Maria is feminine, so the participle ends in -a: è arrivata.

activities.en: Yesterday Marco came home early.

blanks.explanation: Tornare takes essere, and Marco is masculine: è tornato.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.it: Ciao! Ieri sera ti ho chiamato, ma non hai risposto. Cosa hai fatto?
turns.en: Hi! I called you last night, but you didn't answer. What did you do?

turns.speaker: you
turns.en: Sorry! I ____.

blanks.explanation: A man says sono andato / sono uscito, a woman sono andata / sono uscita.

reactions.it: Al cinema! Hai visto un bel film?
reactions.en: At the cinema! Did you see a good film?

reactions.it: Con gli amici! E dove siete andati?
reactions.en: With friends! And where did you go?

reactions.it: Capisco. E com'è andata?
reactions.en: I see. And how did it go?

turns.speaker: partner
turns.en: And then? Were you out late?

turns.speaker: you
turns.en: Yes, I ____ home at midnight.

blanks.explanation: With essere the participle agrees with you: tornato for a man, tornata for a woman.

reactions.it: A mezzanotte! Allora oggi sei stanco.
reactions.en: At midnight! Then you're tired today.

reactions.it: A mezzanotte! Allora oggi sei stanca.
reactions.en: At midnight! Then you're tired today.

reactions.it: A mezzanotte! Allora oggi hai sonno.
reactions.en: At midnight! Then you're sleepy today.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.en: Come on, let's get a coffee.

activities.en: The girls arrived at the party.

blanks.explanation: Arrivare takes essere: le ragazze sono…
Le ragazze is feminine plural, so the participle ends in -e: arrivate.

activities.hint: First the auxiliary, then the participle that matches the girls.

activities.en: My friends went out last night.
activities.answer: I miei amici sono usciti ieri sera.
accepted: Ieri sera i miei amici sono usciti.
activities.explanation: I miei amici is masculine plural: sono usciti.

activities.template: Sabato ____ al mare con la famiglia.
activities.en: On Saturday I went to the seaside with my family.

blanks.explanation: Andare takes essere. Say andato or andata depending on who you are; andati is for a group.

examples: Io sono andato al mare ieri.
Mia sorella è tornata a casa tardi.
Le ragazze sono restate a casa ieri sera.

lessons.title: Quando?
lessons.outcome: Say when something happened with ieri, la settimana scorsa, due giorni fa.

activities.body: Time markers usually open the sentence or close it: ieri, ieri sera, stamattina, la settimana scorsa, l'anno scorso, due giorni fa. Fa (ago) always comes after the amount of time.

examples.it: Ieri sera ho visto un film.
examples.en: Last night I watched a film.

examples.it: La settimana scorsa siamo andati a Firenze.
examples.en: Last week we went to Florence.

examples.it: Due giorni fa ho comprato un libro.
examples.en: Two days ago I bought a book.

examples.it: Anna ha lavorato a Milano l'anno scorso.
examples.en: Anna worked in Milan last year.

activities.tip: Scorso agrees like an adjective: la settimana scorsa, l'anno scorso, il mese scorso. Stamattina is one word: this morning.

activities.en: Last week we went to Florence.
activities.answer: La settimana scorsa siamo andati a Firenze.
activities.explanation: Settimana is feminine: la settimana scorsa. Andare takes essere: siamo andati.

activities.template: ____ ho mangiato al ristorante con Paolo.
activities.en: Last night I ate at the restaurant with Paolo.

blanks.explanation: Ho mangiato is in the past, so the marker must be a past one: ieri sera.

activities.template: Ho comprato questa macchina due ____ fa.
activities.en: I bought this car two years ago.

blanks.explanation: After due the noun is plural: due anni. Fa comes last: due anni fa = two years ago.

activities.hint: Two of them, so the noun is plural.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.en: Have you ever visited Rome?

blanks.explanation: A time marker alone can answer the question: l'anno scorso, due anni fa, il mese scorso.

reactions.it: L'anno scorso! In estate?
reactions.en: Last year! In summer?

reactions.it: Due anni fa? Allora è ora di tornare!
reactions.en: Two years ago? Then it's time to go back!

reactions.it: La settimana scorsa? Che bello!
reactions.en: Last week? How nice!

reactions.it: Il mese scorso! Con chi?
reactions.en: Last month! With whom?

reactions.it: Che bello! Io non ci sono mai stata.
reactions.en: How nice! I've never been there.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.en: And what did you see?

turns.speaker: you
turns.template: A Roma ____ tanti musei e tante chiese.
turns.en: In Rome I ____ many museums and many churches.

blanks.explanation: Vedere → visto (irregular), visitare → visitato. Abbiamo if you went with someone.

reactions.it: Tanti musei! Ma hai mangiato bene?
reactions.en: So many museums! But did you eat well?

reactions.it: Avete visto tanto! E avete mangiato bene?
reactions.en: You saw a lot! And did you eat well?

reactions.it: Che bello! E hai mangiato bene?
reactions.en: How nice! And did you eat well?

turns.speaker: partner
turns.it: Io voglio andare a Roma il mese prossimo.
turns.en: I want to go to Rome next month.

activities.en: Two days ago I bought a book.
activities.answer: Due giorni fa ho comprato un libro.
accepted: Ho comprato un libro due giorni fa.
activities.explanation: Due giorni fa: the amount of time first, then fa. Comprare takes avere, not sono.

activities.en: This morning Marco arrived in Milan by train.

blanks.explanation: Stamattina = this morning, which is already past.
Arrivare takes essere, and Marco is masculine: è arrivato.

activities.en: I saw Anna yesterday.
activities.explanation: The time marker can also close the sentence: ho visto Anna ieri. With avere the participle stays visto.

examples: Io ho visitato un museo la settimana scorsa.
Anna ha comprato un libro due giorni fa.
I miei genitori hanno visto la città l'anno scorso.

lessons.title: Era così
lessons.outcome: Set the scene in the past with the imperfetto, then report one event.

activities.body: The imperfetto paints the background: how things were, the weather, habits (era, c'era, faceva, avevo, andavo). The one thing that happened is in the passato prossimo.

examples.en: It was late and it was cold.
There were a lot of people in the square.
As a child I had a dog. (a man speaking)
While I was sleeping, Marco arrived.

activities.tip: Imperfetto endings: -avo, -evo, -ivo (io); -ava, -eva, -iva (lui, lei); -avamo, -evamo, -ivamo (noi); -avano, -evano, -ivano (loro). Essere is irregular: ero, eri, era, eravamo, eravate, erano.

activities.template: Ieri ____ freddo e non c'era il sole.
activities.en: Yesterday it was cold and there was no sun.

blanks.explanation: Non c'era il sole sets the scene, so the cold goes in the imperfetto too: faceva freddo.

activities.en: As a child Marco had a dog.
activities.answer: Da bambino Marco aveva un cane.
activities.explanation: A state that lasted (he had a dog) takes the imperfetto: aveva, not ha avuto.

activities.template: Quando Anna è arrivata, ____ molta gente alla festa.
activities.en: When Anna arrived, there were a lot of people at the party.

blanks.explanation: Gente is singular in Italian: c'era molta gente. The crowd is the background; the arrival is the event.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.en: What was your first school like?

turns.speaker: you
turns.en: It ____ small, but nice.

blanks.explanation: Describing how something was takes the imperfetto: era.

reactions.it: Anche la mia era piccola!
reactions.en: Mine was small too!

reactions.it: Davvero? Capisco.
reactions.en: Really? I see.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.it: E cosa facevi dopo la scuola?
turns.en: And what did you do after school?

turns.speaker: you
turns.template: Dopo la scuola ____ con gli amici.
turns.en: After school I ____ with my friends.

blanks.explanation: A habit in the past (what you used to do) takes the imperfetto: giocavo, studiavo.

reactions.it: Anche io giocavo sempre!
reactions.en: I always played too!

reactions.it: Dopo la scuola? Io non studiavo mai!
reactions.en: After school? I never studied!

reactions.it: Davvero? Io giocavo sempre.
reactions.en: Really? I always played.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.en: And where was your house?

turns.speaker: you
turns.template: La mia casa ____ vicino alla scuola.
turns.en: My house ____ near the school.

blanks.explanation: Where something was, as a lasting state: era.

reactions.it: Comodo! Io invece abitavo lontano.
reactions.en: Convenient! I lived far away instead.

reactions.it: Capisco. Io invece abitavo lontano.
reactions.en: I see. I lived far away instead.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.en: Good times!

activities.en: While I was sleeping, Marco arrived.

blanks.explanation: Mentre + imperfetto for the action in progress: mentre dormivo.
The event that interrupts is in the passato prossimo: è arrivato.

activities.en: When we were little, we went to the seaside.
activities.answer: Quando eravamo piccoli, andavamo al mare.
activities.explanation: A repeated habit (every summer) takes the imperfetto: andavamo, not siamo andati.

examples: Io avevo un cane a quel tempo.
Mio nonno leggeva molti libri la sera.
I bambini guardavano la televisione ogni giorno.

lessons.title: Raccontami
lessons.outcome: Tell what happened yesterday in a conversation, mixing events and background.

activities.body: A story in the past says when (ieri), what happened in order (prima…, poi…), and how things were (era, c'era, faceva).

examples.it: Ieri è stata una bella giornata.
examples.en: Yesterday was a lovely day.

examples.it: Prima ho lavorato, poi sono uscito con Anna.
examples.en: First I worked, then I went out with Anna. (a man speaking)
We ate together at the restaurant.

examples.it: Era tardi, ma siamo tornati a casa a piedi.
examples.en: It was late, but we walked home.

activities.tip: Prima… poi… puts events in order. For the background (the weather, the time, how you felt) switch to the imperfetto.

activities.en: First we worked, then we went out.
activities.answer: Prima abbiamo lavorato, poi siamo usciti.
activities.explanation: Lavorare takes avere; uscire takes essere and agrees with noi: siamo usciti.

activities.en: Yesterday was a lovely day.

blanks.explanation: Both work: è stata reports the day as a finished event, era describes it. Essere never takes ha.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.en: So, tell me! How did it go yesterday?

turns.speaker: you
turns.en: Good! Yesterday morning I ____ early.

blanks.explanation: Alzarsi and uscire take essere and agree with you (alzato / alzata); lavorare takes avere.

reactions.it: Presto? Bravo! Io invece ho dormito molto.
reactions.en: Early? Well done! I slept a lot instead.

reactions.it: Presto? Brava! Io invece ho dormito molto.
reactions.en: Early? Well done! I slept a lot instead.

reactions.it: Di mattina presto? Che giornata lunga!
reactions.en: Early in the morning? What a long day!

reactions.it: Presto! Con chi?
reactions.en: Early! With whom?

reactions.it: Davvero? Io invece ho dormito molto.
reactions.en: Really? I slept a lot instead.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.en: And afterwards? What did you do?

turns.speaker: you
turns.en: Afterwards I ____ with Marco.

blanks.explanation: Pranzare, parlare and studiare take avere; uscire takes essere and agrees with you.

reactions.it: Con Marco! Lui mangia sempre tanto.
reactions.en: With Marco! He always eats a lot.

reactions.it: Con Marco! Lui è simpatico.
reactions.en: With Marco! He's nice.

reactions.it: Con Marco! Lui parla sempre tanto.
reactions.en: With Marco! He always talks a lot.

reactions.it: Avete studiato insieme? Bravi!
reactions.en: You studied together? Well done!

reactions.it: Con Marco! Che bello.
reactions.en: With Marco! How nice.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.en: And what was the weather like?

turns.speaker: you
turns.en: It ____ hot and the sun was out.

blanks.explanation: Weather uses fare in the imperfetto: faceva caldo. C'era il sole: the sun was out.

reactions.it: Che bella giornata!
reactions.en: What a lovely day!

reactions.it: Una giornata di sole, allora.
reactions.en: A sunny day, then.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.it: E la sera? Cosa avete fatto?
turns.en: And in the evening? What did you do?

turns.speaker: you
turns.template: La sera ____ a casa e ____ un film.
turns.en: In the evening we ____ home and ____ a film.

blanks.explanation: Noi with an essere verb: tornati for a mixed or male group, tornate for women only.
Vedere → visto, guardare → guardato, both with avere: abbiamo visto.

reactions.it: A casa! Una serata tranquilla, allora.
reactions.en: Home! A quiet evening, then.

reactions.it: A casa tutta la sera? Bello anche così.
reactions.en: At home all evening? Nice that way too.

reactions.it: Che bella giornata! La prossima volta vengo anche io.
reactions.en: What a lovely day! Next time I'm coming too.

activities.template: Quando Marco ____ a casa, ____ già tardi.
activities.en: When Marco got home, it was already late.

blanks.explanation: The event: è arrivato or è tornato, with essere.
The background (the time of day): era già tardi.

activities.en: Last night we ate together at the restaurant.
activities.answer: Ieri sera abbiamo mangiato insieme al ristorante.
accepted: Abbiamo mangiato insieme al ristorante ieri sera.
activities.explanation: Mangiare takes avere: abbiamo mangiato, not siamo.

activities.template: Due giorni fa ____ i miei nonni.
activities.en: Two days ago I saw my grandparents.

blanks.explanation: A single completed event takes the passato prossimo with avere: ho visto (vedere has the irregular participle visto), not vedevo (a habit) or sono visto (wrong auxiliary).

examples: Io ho cenato al ristorante ieri sera.
I miei genitori sono tornati a casa la settimana scorsa.
Noi siamo restati a casa sabato.
